architecture.coreLaw: Cognition attempt identity is not progress authority. A successor attempt may lawfully reset attempt-local cognition while retaining the same exact selected WorkingSet pins, but that attempt reset does not by itself constitute structural progress.
architecture.progressAuthority: Soft observation/no-progress authority is carried by durable remaining-budget counters. The process-local external-observation gate reason is a derived projection and is reconstructed from those counters after fresh-process resume.
architecture.selectionProgress: A WorkingSet transition whose exact selected pin tuple differs from the current committed selection is structural cognition progress. It may reset observation-only/no-progress counters and reopen a soft external-effect gate. A transition with the same exact pins does neither.
architecture.attemptReset: Same-selection successor attempts remain legal because attempt identity owns transient cognition lifetime. They still clear predecessor attempt-local Tool exchanges and begin a fresh cognition attempt while preserving the durable source selection.
architecture.hardBudget: Hard Tool-call budget remains global Run authority. Neither same-selection attempt reset nor selected-pin mutation can revive consumed Tool-call budget.
architecture.resumeLaw: Fresh-process resume without new model-visible cognition recomputes the closed soft gate from durable counters rather than reopening capability because process identity changed.
architecture.effectiveCognitionLaw: A canonical Run message is not automatically cognition progress. In the current projected WorkingView path, resume additional_messages are retained in canonical history but lack a proven Provider-visible WorkingView ingress; they therefore do not reset soft progress merely by existing. The non-projected path continues to send appended caller messages in the Provider-visible transcript and retains its existing resume behavior.
architecture.schemaChange: No SQLite schema, Protocol codec, new progress database, generic cognition state machine or recommended public API was added.

behavior.sameSelectionClosedGateAttack: With maxObservationOnlyTurns=1, an observation-only Runtime search closed the soft external-effect gate. The Agent then committed a fresh successor attempt with the same exact pins and requested a second Runtime search. Before P-C1.9 the attempt reset reopened Tools and allowed a second physical dispatch. After P-C1.9 the transition remains committed, its predecessor Tool exchange is discarded, but the third Provider request still exposes no Runtime Tool surface; the second Tool request is stopped before effect. Runtime physical dispatch remains one.
behavior.sameSelectionPreGateAttack: With maxObservationOnlyTurns=2, one observation-only search consumed one soft-progress unit, a same-selection attempt reset occurred, and a second observation-only search followed. The reset no longer restores the counter: the second search reaches the original two-turn threshold and the subsequent closure turn has no Runtime Tool surface.
behavior.selectionChangeControl: After a soft gate closed, an Agent transition from [A] to [A,B] reset soft progress because the exact selected cognition changed. A subsequent Runtime observation was admitted. This prevents the fix from incorrectly treating every cognition transition as a no-op.
behavior.hardBudgetControl: With maxToolCalls=1, one Runtime effect exhausted the hard Tool budget. A later structural selection change from [A] to [A,B] did not revive Tool capability; a second requested Tool effect was stopped with zero additional Runtime dispatch.
behavior.transientResetControl: A same-selection successor attempt following a Tool exchange still projects only the durable base source on the next turn. The predecessor assistant Tool-call message and Tool Observation disappear, proving that same-selection attempt reset remains a real cognition-lifecycle action despite not being progress.
behavior.freshResumeAttack: A Run paused after an observation-only turn had already closed the soft gate. A fresh Store/Continuity/Loop resumed without caller input. Before P-C1.9 the restored counters existed but the process-local gate string was empty, so Runtime Tools reappeared. After P-C1.9 the first resumed Provider request has an empty Runtime Tool surface and Continuity Doctor remains healthy.
behavior.projectedCallerInputFinding: A projected WorkingView resume with additional caller text was inspected directly. The caller text is present in canonical Run state but absent from the Provider-visible projected request. P-C1.9 therefore does not allow that invisible message to reset soft progress. This exposes a separate caller-input-to-WorkingView ingress problem rather than silently counting canonical state mutation as Agent cognition progress.
behavior.nonProjectedCompatibility: The existing non-projected needs_input snapshot resume test still passes: appended caller input remains part of the next Provider-visible transcript and the legacy path continues to complete normally.
behavior.liveDeepSeek: One live deepseek-v4-flash probe repeated the P-C1.8 recall setup. The model called inspect_working_set_history and identified the correct K pin, but its next transition reused the current attempt identity instead of proposing a fresh successor. The existing new-attempt-identity law rejected the model output before transition admission. Because the run never reached a same-selection successor under P-C1.9, this live probe is recorded as inconclusive for the new progress boundary and is not used as positive acceptance evidence.

conclusion: P-C1.9 separates cognition lifecycle from progress authority. Attempt identity may change solely to discard attempt-local cognition while retaining the same durable selected sources; this remains a lawful Agent action but no longer resets progress counters or renews external-effect capability. Structural progress is the exact selected-pin mutation, while hard effect budgets remain independent and monotonic. Soft gate authority now survives process replacement because it is derived from durable counters rather than a process-local string. The experiments also exposed that projected resume caller messages are not currently model-visible; P-C1.9 deliberately stops treating those invisible canonical messages as progress instead of inventing a new overlay. A separate caller-input cognition-ingress experiment is required next.
knownLimits: Progress is structural, not semantic. Harness compares exact selected WorkingSet pins; it does not prove whether two different sources contain equivalent information or whether a selection change is strategically useful.
An Agent can still oscillate between different exact selections. P-C1.9 does not add semantic equivalence detection, historical selection novelty scoring, or a cognition-transition frequency policy.

Same-selection attempt reset remains legal and may be used repeatedly until ordinary model/token/wall-time limits stop the Run. P-C1.9 prevents it from renewing soft external-effect progress but does not prohibit cognition churn itself.
Harness-local cognition controls such as WorkingSet history remain separate from Runtime external-effect gates and are still bounded primarily by model/observation/token limits.

Projected WorkingView resume currently lacks a proven ingress for appended caller messages. Those messages are canonical Run history but are not model-visible through the current projector, so they cannot yet serve as progress authority. This is intentionally left for the next experiment rather than solved by an unproven arbitrary-message overlay.
Non-projected resume caller messages remain Provider-visible under the existing canonical transcript path; P-C1.9 does not remove that behavior.
The live deepseek-v4-flash probe did not reach a valid P-C1.9 same-selection successor because the model reused the current attempt ID and was rejected by the existing transition identity law.
No Runtime, World, Finance or Host repository was changed.
